messages:
maya: heads up — seeing a KV-cache regen storm in eu-west that lines up with a big tenant replay. p50 token latency jumped 2.3x for small inference jobs.
aj: ugh. any correlation with slab churn or prefetch misses?
maya: slab churn yes, prefetch hitrate tanked to ~12% (normal ~66%). logs show repeated full-cache invalidations from tenant T-1123.
leo: ops-bot just flagged a spike earlier — can we paste the alert?
ops-bot: ALERT: kvcache_invalidation_rate high on eu-west-rack-7 (90th percentile) — 2024-06-11T09:21Z — recent history: 4x baseline, triggered autoscale? false.
nora: is this the same tenant that did large batch replays yesterday? saw big replay window 03:00-04:00 UTC.
maya: yep. T-1123 runs heavy sampling job that iterates model prefixes; it accidentally set prefetch=false in their client iteration so every request mis-hits and causes regeneration.
aj: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) rate-limit invalidation events per-tenant 2) soft-shield: route that tenant to a dedicated mini-pool 3) increase kvcache eviction TTLs to make regen less frequent
samir: +1 for (1) as a low-risk quick fix. we can clamp invalidation events in proxy with a token bucket per-tenant. cheap to roll.
leo: do we have an existing per-tenant quota proxy hook? I can whip a small envoy filter but needs testing.
ora: we should also consider adaptive prefetch fallback: if hitrate < 30% for 2 min, flip to prefetch=true path and throttle regen. but that's more invasive.
maya: created a quick probe: curl -sS http://controlplane.internal/debug/kvcache?tenant=T-1123 | jq '.stats | {hitrate, invalidations_per_min}' yields: {"hitrate": 0.12, "invalidations_per_min": 48}
aj: ok implement token-bucket clamp to 5 invalidations/min for T-1123 and similar bursty tenants. can we rollout as a proxy feature flag?
leo: yes I can do a canary in eu-west-rack-7. filter pseudo-config: ```
// envoy lua snippet
local tenant = request:headers()["x-tenant-id"]
if get_bucket(tenant):consume(1) == false then
  return respond(429, "kvcache-invalidation-rate-limit")
end
```
samir: 429s are fine short term; clients should retry with jitter. but let's avoid 429s for important customers — route to dedicated mini-pool for premium.
nora: cost impact: shielding/pinning to dedicated pool will increase GPU-hours for that tenant. estimate: pinning T-1123 for 12h would cost ~+$1200 for eu-west. add to incident budget?
maya: agree. for now we'll do clamp + notify tenant to fix client. message drafted: "we saw client pattern causing regen storms; please enable prefetch or reduce invalidation frequency".
aj: owners: leo (proxy canary), samir (policy rollout), maya (tenant comms). plan: 1) proxy clamp canary in eu-west-rack-7 (10m) 2) if stable, widen to eu-west region (30m) 3) offer dedicated slice for premium if they need sustained throughput.
leo: starting PR for envoy filter, will attach test logs. target deploy in 15m.
maya: ping T-1123 support contact now.
ops-bot: INCIDENT_NOTE: mitigation started by leo at 2024-06-11T09:28Z — proxy clamp canary applied to rack-7. Observability: watching prefetch hitrate and overall p50.
aj: quick dashboards to watch: kvcache.hitrate, kvcache.invalidations_per_min (by tenant), p50_inference_latency (eu-west), gpu_util by pool.
samir: after clamp, we should produce a long-term: adaptive invalidation smoothing + per-tenant regen budget with billing signals. leaves a TODO in infra roadmap.
maya: thanks team — will follow up with tenant and update thread in 30m. :thumbsup:
